sentences.text:
The present revision petition is filed challenging the impugned order dated 24.01.2023 of Ld.
MM-03, West, Delhi in CC No. 3122/2016 PS- Nihal Vihar titled as Dinesh Shokeen Vs Jai Prakash Chauhan and ors. whereby the complaint case filed by the complainant U/s 200 Cr.P.C was dismissed holding that no case for the alleged offence was made out.

sentences.text:
The revisionist herein is the complainant before the Ld. Trial Court while the respondents no. 1 to 4 are the proposed accused no.
1 to 4 before the Ld. Trial Court.
For the sake of convenience, parties shall be referred to by their nomenclature before Ld. Trial Court.

BRIEF FACTS:
2. Brief facts of the case necessary for disposal of the present revision petition are that the complainant filed a complaint case U/s 200 Cr.P.C before the Ld. Trial Court against four proposed a c c u s e d p e r s o n s a l l e g i n g c o m m i s s i o n o f o f f e n c e s U / s 323/325/341/379/384/419/420/427/452/465/467/468/471/506/120B /34 IPC.
The complaint was accompanied with an application U/s 156(3) Cr.P.C seeking directions for registration of FIR.
The said application was dismissed vide order dated 24.07.2014 and complainant was called upon to lead pre-summoning evidence.

3. The allegations made in the complaint are that complainant is the owner of plot no. D-2/43,
Kunwar Singh Nagar, Nangloi admeasuring 200 sq. yds which was purchased by him vide registered GPA etc. dated 13.07.2006 from Sh Kuriakose J. Vari.
He is also owner of adjacent plot no. D-2/43A admeasuring 63 sq. yds purchased from one Sachin Kumar Bhardwaj vide GPA etc all dated 23.03.2006.
Proposed accused no. 1 Jai Prakash Chauhan is stated to be the owner and in possession of adjacent house no. D- 2/44 admeasuring 274 sq. yds and having an evil eye on the plot of the complainant.

It is stated that alleged accused no. 1 in connivance with proposed accused no. 4 forged a false agreement to sell of plot no. D-2/44 which was found to be forged by CFSL in a criminal complaint filed by him.
Proposed accused no. 1 is alleged to be a land grabber and a habitual litigant in the habit of making false complaints to police and courts.
It is alleged that he has been making false complaints against the complainant to forcibly take possession of complainant's properties.

4. It is further alleged that on 04.08.2013 in the morning, when parents of the complainant reached his plot, they were shocked to see that alleged accused no. 1, 2 & 3 had removed the gate of the plot and nearby boundary wall by breaking it and were getting fixed railing on the back side wall of the plot.
They informed the complainant telephonically which annoyed proposed accused no 1.
Proposed accused no. 1 to 3 restrained the parents of complainant and started beating them and also threatened to kill them.
Proposed accused no. 1 also tried to molest the mother of complainant by touching her breast and trying to tear her clothes.
The complainant reached the spot and tried to save his parents but his mother was beaten with a danda and her knee was injured.
Alleged accused no. 1 to 3 also started giving beatings to the complainant and caused fracture on his finger.
Complainant called the police at 100 number and he and his mother were rushed to SGM hospital.
Their statements were recorded by the police but only a case u/s 354B IPC was registered on the complaint of mother of complainant but other allegations were not paid any heed.
Alleged accused no. 1 was orally asked to stop the construction work.

sentences.text: On 11.08.2013, father of complainant got information that alleged accused no. 1 was fixing the gate in place of broken gate and he reached the spot.
However, father of complainant was made to sit in the Police Station since morning and alleged accused no. 1 was given an opportunity to complete the construction.
At that time, complainant was hospitalized.
Father of the complainant reported the matter at 100 number but police did not take any action.
Complaints were made to the police and higher authorities but no action was taken against the alleged accused persons.

Hence,the present complaint was filed U/s 200 Cr.P.C.
PRE-SUMMONING EVIDENCE 6.
Complainant examined two witnesses in his pre-summoning evidence.
He examined himself as CW1 and stated on oath the allegations made in the complaint.

He relied upon an irrevocable GPA dated 13.07.2006 executed in his favour by one Kuriakose J. Vari in respect of plot no. 43 admeasuring 200 sq. yds out of Khasra no. 28/1 and 29/5 situated in the area of village Kamruddin Nagar, Nangloi, Delhi-41 abadi known as Kunwar Singh Nagar which is Ex. CW-1/A; and complaints made to SHO/DCP which are Ex. CW-1/2 (colly).

He also deposed that proposed accused no.1 had got prepared false and fabricated documents that are agreement to sell dated 15.2.2000 in respect of plot no. 44 admeasuring 252 sq yds out of Khasra no. 29/5 situated in the revenue estate of village Kamruddin Nagar, Delhi and abadi known as Kunwar Singh Nagar, Block D-2, Delhi -41 which is Mark A in which proposed accused no. 4 had stood as a witness which is alleged to have been executed by mother of complainant Smt Kitabo Devi.

He alleged that thumb impression/signature of Smt Kitabo Devi on document Mark A were forged and fabricated and FSL result in this regard has already been obtained by the police officials in case FIR 127/11 P.S Nihal Vihar.
7. Father of complainant Sh Anoop Singh is examined as CW2.
He deposed in consonance with the testimony of CW1.
IMPUGNED ORDER 8.

After hearing the arguments on summoning, Ld. Trial Court vide impugned order dated 24.01.2023 held that no ground for summoning of any of accused persons was made out as from the submissions as well as deposition produced on record, no case for alleged commission of offence was made out.
Thus the complaint case was dismissed.

GROUNDS FOR REVISION/ARGUMENTS OF COMPLAINANT:
9.
The impugned order has been challenged stating that it is bad in law and has been passed on assumptions and presumptions.

Ld Trial Court has failed to take into consideration the FSL report filed by complainant in respect of forged and fabricated agreement to sell as well as the fact that forged and fabricated agreement to sell was produced in the Court by alleged accused no.1 himself.
10. Ld counsel for complainant has argued in line with the grounds of appeal and has sought setting aside of the impugned order.

sentences.text:
ARGUMENTS OF THE RESPONDENT/ALLEGED ACCUSED PERSONS:
11.
Per contra, the present revision petition has been vehemently opposed on behalf of respondents.
It is submitted that impugned order is a well reasoned order passed on the basis of material available on record and evidence produced by the complainant.
The present revision petition fails to point out any infirmity or illegality in the impugned order.

Ld. Trial Court has rightly observed that it is an admitted case of the complainant that proposed accused no. 1 is the owner of plot no.
D-2/44, however, in his evidence he is alleging that the document of said plot executed in favour of proposed accused no 1 are forged and fabricated.
In these circumstances, dismissal of present revision petition is sought.
FINDINGS 12.
I have heard the submissions made and carefully perused the record.

By way of complaint U/s 200 Cr P.C complainant had reported about two incidents dated 04.08.2013 and 11.08.2013 when he and his family members were allegedly manhandled by proposed accused persons and proposed accused no. 1 had tried to forcibly enter into and take possession of his property bearing plot no.D-2/43 and D-2/43A.
It is the own case of complainant and specifically pleaded in Paragraph no.2 of his complaint that alleged accused no. 1 is the owner and in possession of plot no. D-2/44.
There are no allegations in the complaint U/s 200 Cr.P.C or prior complaints made to the police officials that forgery of any alleged sale deed in favour of proposed accused no. 1 was being reported.

The complaint even does not mention any details of the allegedly forged sale documents in favour of proposed accused no. 1 or the details of the FSL report as per which the said sale documents were forged.
However, when the complainant stepped into the witness box, he produced agreement to sell dated 15.02.2000 (Mark A) alleging it to be forged and fabricated.
In the same breath, he also stated that FSL result in respect of the said agreement to sell has already been obtained by the police officials in case FIR no. 127/11 P.S Nihal Vihar.

There is no clarity that when the said agreement to sell is already a subject matter of case FIR no. 127/11 P.S Nihal Vihar, why its forgery is being highlighted in the pre-summoning evidence of this case.
In addition to this, no such FSL report showing the agreement to sell (Mark A) to be a forged document has been proved on record by the complainant.
Accordingly, the findings of Ld. Trial Court on this aspect are well reasoned and based on the evidence and material produced by the complainant.

No ground is made out for summoning of proposed accused persons on the basis of the allegations of forgery of agreement to sell dated 15.02.2000 (MarkA).
13.

As regard the incident dated 04.08.2023 detailed in the complaint U/s 200 CrPC, none of the witnesses examined at pre summoning stage has supported the said incident in their testimonies as CW1 and CW2.
Even otherwise, the complaint itself mentions in paragraph no. 6 that a case u/s 354B IPC was registered qua the said incident dated 04.08.2023.

As regards the incident dated 11.8.2023, the complainant himself is not a witness to the said incident while the testimony of his father/CW2 is only to the effect that he had seen the alleged accused no. 1 fixing gate in place of a broken gate at plot no. D-2/43 and he had called the police at 100 number and he himself was taken to the P.S.
Thus, even CW-2 is not a witness to what had actually transpired at the spot on 11.8.2023 as he was at the P.S.

There is no evidence on record to support the fact that alleged accused no. 1 had actually taken possession of plot belonging to complainant nor there is any deposition of complainant's witnesses to this effect.

Thus, from the evidence produced on record at the pre Dinesh Shokeen vs Jai Prakash Chauhan on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17909022/
4 summoning stage, no sufficient ground for proceeding further in the matter is made out.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the summoning of accused persons has been rightly rejected by the Ld. Trial Court and the complaint has been rightly dismissed U/s 203 Cr.P.C.
14.
In view of the reasons given above, I am of the opinion that there is no infirmity or illegality in the impugned order dated 24.01.2023.
No ground is made out for interfering with the same as from the evidence produced on record there is no sufficient ground for proceeding further by summoning the alleged accused persons.
The present revision petition is therefore, dismissed and impugned order dated 24.01.2023 is upheld.
15. TCR be sent back to the Ld. Trial Court alongwith a copy of this order.
16. Revision file be consigned to Record Room.
